html:
SMTO-BOOT-0006 — Your account can't update the Gateway's installed files

GUID: 0603ffa4-ed96-4034-a4df-202fe7290d75
Slug: boot-environment-readonly
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The Gateway installer found the Gateway's existing program files, but your user account isn't allowed to change them, often because a different account or sudo installed them before. The Gateway's program files weren't updated.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run the Gateway installer as the same user account that installed the Gateway before, usually the account that normally starts it. Only the account that owns those files can update them safely.
  2. If you're not sure who owns them, ask the person who manages this computer to check the owner of the .venv folder inside src/gateway_agent (or src/gateway_macos on a Mac). That folder is exactly the one the installer needs to change.
  3. If those files should belong to you, have that person give your account ownership of just that .venv folder, then run the installer again. Fixing only that folder solves the problem without opening up the rest of the computer.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway installer finishes with a completion message, and the Gateway starts with its startup command.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal message, including the Error reference line, and send it to the person who manages this computer. Don't run everything with sudo or make the folder writable by everyone; that weakens the computer's security.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway installer found an existing src/gateway_agent/.venv or src/gateway_macos/.venv directory that is not writable by the current account and stopped before updating it.

What this means

  • Gateway installation finds an existing virtual-environment directory that is not writable by the current account. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway installation finds an existing virtual-environment directory that is not writable by the current account.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact environment owner and required write permissions without broad permission changes.

How to fix it

  • Check ownership with ls -ld on the Gateway's .venv and rerun the installer as the owning account, or deliberately chown only that directory tree to the account that runs the Gateway. Avoid sudo installs, chmod -R 777 or other broad permission changes, and preserve the Gateway's pairing and state files.
  • Run the installer as the environment’s owning account or deliberately repair its ownership/permissions. Preserve application state and avoid broad permission changes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended owning account can update that environment while preserving application state.

What not to do

  • Do not grant broad permissions; verify the exact resource, identity and required access.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
